items.text:
Medvedev beat Cobolli in straight sets in Turin, where Cobolli was playing the event for the first time and he needed only two sets to do it.

The first set stayed on serve all the way. Medvedev had five break points in it, early in the set and again at 4–4 but Cobolli saved them all and held each time. Medvedev did not let those missed chances bother him and was too solid in the tiebreak, which he took 7–4 to lead by a set. The second set was tight until he finally broke for 4–3. From there he held and broke once more in the last game, winning 4 games in a row to take the set 6–3 and the match.

Those breaks came late but Medvedev was never in trouble on his own serve. His first serve worked very well and he did not face a single break point all match. On the other side, Cobolli really struggled behind his second serve.

Overall, the gap between the two was clear on a quick indoor hard court that suited Medvedev and a dominance ratio of 1.86 shows how much more he got out of the points than Cobolli. Next is Alcaraz.

items.text: I've always said that I'm not bad on indoor courts … It's just that it seemed to me that other players were a bit better than me. It was just a matter of time, of gaining more experience, of understanding how I had to play on indoor courts. I think I'm almost there. I'm starting to understand how I should play indoors. I've gained more experience. Every time I play on this surface I also gain confidence. I'm really happy to show everyone that I can play great tennis here. I can hold my own against anyone with powerful, flat serves and shots, and be able to win those kinds of matches. I'm just happy to see that I'm reaching the level I always thought I could reach
items.originalText: Ho sempre detto che non me la cavo male sui campi al coperto … È solo che mi sembrava che altri giocatori fossero un po’ più bravi di me. Era solo questione di tempo , di fare più esperienza, di capire come dovevo giocare sui campi al coperto. Penso di esserci quasi. Sto cominciando a capire come dovrei giocare indoor . Ho acquisito più esperienza. Ogni volta che gioco su questa superficie acquisisco anche sicurezza. Sono davvero felice di dimostrare a tutti che qui riesco a giocare un ottimo tennis. Posso tenere testa a chiunque con servizi e colpi potenti, piatti, ed essere in grado di vincere quel tipo di partite. Sono semplicemente felice di vedere che sto raggiungendo il livello che ho sempre pensato di poter raggiungere

items.text:
Alcaraz beat Tiafoe 6–2, 6–2 in Turin in just 68 minutes, a near perfect display that was strong in every part of his game.

He made a very fast start and broke Tiafoe's serve more than once early in the opening set. Tiafoe had a very hard first six games and never really got back into it, while Alcaraz changed direction easily from cross-court to down the line and sped up in the middle of points to win them. He took the first set 6–2 and was one set away from the win.

It was the same story in the second set. An early break put him in front again and although Tiafoe showed fine touch at times, Alcaraz stayed one step ahead and finished with a dominance ratio of 2.06.

Even the one moment of danger went his way. Tiafoe finally had his chance with 3 break points but Alcaraz saved all of them and held, then broke once more to take the set 6–2 and the match. On the big points he gave nothing away. Next is Medvedev.

items.text:
Shelton beat Fils in three sets at the ATP Finals and it was his first ever win at this event.

He played a very strong first set. Fils got out of an early game on his serve but Shelton broke him twice after that and won 5 games in a row to take it 6–2, mixing big serves into the body with wide ones. Fils pushed hard in the second set and won some of the best points of the match. He broke late, then had to save break points while he served for the set but he held to take it 6–3 and make it one set all.

The deciding set turned early. Shelton broke for 2–0, though it took him several chances in that game and then had to protect that lead. Fils had two chances to break back before Shelton held for 4–1 and Fils got one more look when Shelton served for the match. Shelton held again and won the set 6–3. Credit to him: once he was ahead in the third, he never gave the break back.

68% behind his second serve shows why Fils found it so hard to break him, far above his 53% average on hard. His backhand was a real weapon too, with several clean winners.

Shelton did what he had to do but it was not perfect: he made 32 unforced errors and that is what he has to clean up for the next match. He plays Jodar next.

Shelton: performance rating 8.8 | W: 28 / UE: 32 | DR: 1.37

Fils: performance rating 8.1 | W: 21 / UE: 22 | DR: 0.73

items.topic: On his ATP Finals loss to Zverev

items.text:
Zverev beat Jodar in straight sets in the opening singles match of the week in Turin, against a 20-year-old who was playing the event for the first time.

It was not easy for either of them. The ball was not flying through the air on this fast indoor court and both players seemed to struggle at times to control it. Jodar held well early on but Zverev broke him late in the first set and served for it. Jodar had two break points in that game, the only chances he got all match and Zverev saved both to take the set 6–4. The second set followed the same pattern. Zverev broke early, did not see another break point and took it 6–4 as well.

That serve was the whole story, because Jodar barely got a look at it. Zverev won 86% of the points behind his first serve, against his 74% average on hard. He was also the more clutch of the two on the big points.

It was not perfect but it did not need to be. It was not his best return performance and he let most of his break points go. Still, one break in each set was enough and the moment that decided it came when he held while serving for the first set. Shelton waits in his next match.

Zverev: W: 21 / UE: 18 | DR: 2.01

Jodar: W: 12 / UE: 10 | DR: 0.50
